description:
Follows defk-6lr (and defk-8qs). Short kernel calls fanned out from one process (Task.async_stream) stay on 2-4 of 12 schedulers because a kernel charges 4000 reductions per 250 us slice and ERTS wakes idle schedulers by reductions run on a crowded queue. A shorter slice spreads them (DEFK_SLICE_US 50: 12 schedulers) but costs a lone call 11-18%.

Experiment: choose the slice per call from the run queue. Before the call (in the generated Elixir wrapper, or in the NIF if ERTS exposes it), check whether the caller's scheduler run queue has other runnable processes waiting; only then run the kernel with a short slice (e.g. 50 us, or short for the first ~1 ms), else keep 250 us. Candidates for the check: :erlang.statistics(:run_queue_lengths) (per scheduler; cost?), :erlang.statistics(:total_run_queue_lengths), :erlang.system_info(:scheduler_id) plus a per-scheduler counter, or anything cheaper; measure each one's cost per call. The slice must become a runtime parameter of the call (today DEFK_SLICE_US is a compile-time constant in priv/defk_runtime.h).

Measure on a quiet machine (no other agents; record load): (1) cost of the check per call; (2) single-call speed vs today for short (0.65 ms) and long (2M count_primes) calls; (3) tick gap (bench/tick_gap.exs) with short slices; (4) spread and wall time for 48 x 0.65 ms tasks under Task.async_stream, Task.async + await_many, and 12 x 0.55 ms; (5) the three affected examples (batched_levenshtein, monte_carlo_rtp at 1M, cosine_topk 100k 12 chunks) vs default and +swt very_low. Interleave treatments, medians, as in defk-8qs.

Adopt only if the check costs well under 1% of a 0.65 ms call and most of the spread is recovered; otherwise record the numbers, keep the guidance (examples/README.md rule 7, docs/performance.md 4.1-4.3) as the answer, and leave the code unchanged. Done when the decision is recorded with the measurements in docs/performance.md section 4 and on defk-6lr, and defk-6lr is closed either way.

comments.text:
Decision: ADOPTED as the default (defk-04y). A yielding kernel's function now calls its NIF __defk_native_<name>__ with :erlang.statistics(:total_run_queue_lengths) as an extra last argument; a value > 0 makes the call yield every 50 us (DEFK_SHORT_SLICE_US) for its first 1 ms (DEFK_SHORT_FOR_US), then 250 us as before (defk_slice_init in priv/defk_runtime.h). `use Defk, adaptive_slice: false` opts out. Kernels that never yield are unchanged.

Measured on OTP 29.0.3, 12 schedulers, load average 2.2-2.9 at the start of each block (4-5 during some); treatments interleaved in one VM, medians, two sessions.
(1) Check cost per call (idle / 11 schedulers busy): total_run_queue_lengths 7.8 / 9.3 ns; own queue (run_queue_lengths + nth scheduler_id) 60 / 81 ns; statistics(:run_queue) 43 / 1954 ns; scheduler_id 3 ns. Tiny yielding call count_primes(10): 40-43 -> 49-58 ns (total check), 102-132 ns (own). The NIF API exposes no run-queue length, so the check has to be in Elixir. 9 ns = 0.0014% of a 0.65 ms call.
(2) Lone calls vs 250 us: 0.65 ms -0.6..+0.1% (12 sched), -0.2..-0.1% (1 sched); 2M +0.1..+0.2%: noise. fixed 50 us for the whole call: +8.1% / +7.1% on one scheduler.
(3) Tick gap, one scheduler, 2M count_primes: lone p99 2.25 ms all treatments; with 3 more kernels queued p99 3.2 ms (250 us and adaptive alike; fixed50 2.05). 15 runs of final code: median worst 3.30 ms (250 us) vs 3.34 (adaptive). Slices are never longer than 250 us.
(4) Spread, wall ms / schedulers: 48 x 0.65 ms async_stream 13.6-13.7/3 -> adaptive 5.6-5.7/10-11 (own-queue 5.8-5.9/10, fixed50 5.6-5.7/10-11, +swt very_low 4.4/10-12, Elixir 4.6/11). async+await_many 4.6-5.0/11 -> 4.3-4.5/12. 12 x 0.55 ms 4.2/2 -> 2.1/7 (own 2.4/5, fixed50 2.1/6, swt 1.2-1.3/10-11, Elixir 1.3/11). 48 x 5 ms 35.5-35.7 -> 31.4-31.6 (12 schedulers either way).
(5) Examples (Task.async_stream chunks): batched_levenshtein 12 chunks 3.8-3.9/2 -> 1.9/5-6 (swt 1.0-1.1/9-10); monte_carlo_rtp 1M 48 chunks 12.7/3 -> 5.5/10 (swt 4.6/8-9); cosine_topk 100k 12 chunks 7.7-7.8/5 -> 3.9-4.1/9-10 (swt 3.7/8-9). Recovers 70-93% of what +swt very_low gains; +swt very_low is still 1.1-1.8x better, and bigger chunks / Task.async+await_many stay the first advice.
Didn't help: switching to 50 us inside the kernel after a resume that waited > 20 us (no Elixir check): 12.7/3 vs 13.6/3.

Adoption rule met: the check costs ~0.0014% of a 0.65 ms call, and most of the spread is recovered. Recorded in docs/performance.md 4.9 (4.1/4.3 point to it), docs/guides/runtime-contract.md section 1, examples/README.md rule 7. Benches: bench/run_queue_check_cost.exs, bench/adaptive_slice.exs (single / tick / spread), bench/adaptive_slice_examples.exs; fixed50 and gap columns used the experimental API of commit be24cd7. Tests: test/adaptive_slice_test.exs.

title: Experiment: short slices only when the caller's run queue is crowded (spread short parallel kernel calls without slowing lone calls)
